Rajiv / Samira —

Thanks for confirming VPC peering; below is a concise technical checklist we use to make peering low-friction. I've attached a vpc-peering-template.yml you can drop into your infra repo as a starting point. High level:

1) Redwood org & accounts
   - We'll invite Helix engineers into a dedicated Redwood org (read-only console + admin scopes for Helix admins). Provide a list of users and role mapping (IAM) you want created.

2) API keys and scopes
   - For the POC we'll provision a scoped API key tied to the Helix org (dev/test scope). Keys will be visible in the console; recommend rotating after POC.

3) VPC peering details we need from Helix
   - VPC ID(s) and primary CIDR(s) for peering
   - Route table IDs to accept routes
   - Preferred peering model: route-based peering (managed) or transit (if you have shared services)
   - Whether you require egress NAT from our side or Helix NATs inbound traffic
   - Security groups / ports: we typically require outbound HTTPS (443) plus ephemeral ports 1024-65535 for existing tunnels but will lock this down in the template.
   - ASN if BGP is required for your setup

4) IP allowlist (fallback)
   - If you prefer hosted endpoint with allowlist instead, provide your egress IP blocks. Hosted is typically faster to stand up but a VPC peer will give better security posture.

5) Test plan
   - After peering provisioned we'll run: curl against /health, 10 inference calls with the sample model, perf run (p50/p95) and a true/false content check.

Priyom will set up the infra walkthrough during Tue 4/20 kickoff and can run the peering template line-by-line with Rajiv. If you can send the VPC IDs and route tables ahead of the meeting we can pre-provision on our side and reduce the meeting to 30–45 minutes.

Attachments: vpc-peering-template.yml

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@helixhealth.ai>

Subject: Re: POC connection & org setup — Helix Health MAP & timeline

Karthik / Priyom —

Quick clarifying questions from networking:
- Are you expecting the peering to be "private VPC peering" (AWS) or a transit/VPN solution? We run a shared services transit VPC that prefers attachments via TGW.
- For BGP: do you require ASN exchange or do you plan to do static routes? If ASN is needed our ASN is 64512.
- Ports: we prefer the smallest possible surface. Can you confirm exactly which inbound ports Redwood needs (we want to keep security groups tight)?

I'll upload the VPC IDs and route table IDs to the drive folder after our internal review. If you can share the sample CloudFormation/YAML (you attached vpc-peering-template.yml) with the minimal ports and routes annotated that will help our infra team.

-Rajiv
Network Engineering — Helix Health
rajiv.patel@helixhealth.ai
